turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am not one to be swayed by empty words, Mr. Darcy. You have consistently shown a disregard for those less fortunate than yourself, and I will not be won over by your sudden declarations of love.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am surprised, Elizabeth, that you would so readily judge my character based on a few isolated instances, without considering the many virtues and good deeds that I have performed in my life.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I suppose you expect me to forget the way you treated my sister, and the disdain with which you regarded our family's station, simply because you claim to have undergone a change of heart?

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, Elizabeth, that your harsh judgment is not altogether unexpected, given the... limited understanding of my character that you possess.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I find it curious that you expect me to believe in your sudden conversion, Mr. Darcy, when you have shown so little inclination to change your behavior in the past.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must insist, Elizabeth, that you are not in a position to criticize my behavior, given your own tendency to form judgments based on superficial impressions and your evident lack of understanding of the complexities of high society.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I assure you, Mr. Darcy, that my judgments are not based on superficial impressions, but on the evidence of your actions, and I see no reason to suppose that you have changed in any fundamental way.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, Elizabeth, that your obstinacy in this matter is quite... distressing to me, for I had sincerely hoped that you would see the sincerity of my feelings and the genuine changes that I have undergone.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your professions of love, Mr. Darcy, when your past behavior has been so hurtful and insulting to me and those I care about.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, Elizabeth, that I find your refusal to consider my proposal to be a reflection of your own limited understanding of the world and your own biases against those who possess greater wealth and standing.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am not in the habit of marrying men who have treated my family and me with disdain, Mr. Darcy. Your wealth and standing do not compensate for your lack of character, and I will not be swayed by your attempts to buy my affection.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am astonished, Elizabeth, that you should so callously dismiss the genuine feelings I have expressed, and instead resort to such petty and unfounded accusations against me.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I will not be lectured on my understanding of the world by someone who has consistently shown a lack of empathy and a penchant for condescension. You may have learned to temper your pride, Mr. Darcy, but you have not yet learned to temper your arrogance.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am at a loss to understand, Elizabeth, how you can so thoroughly misunderstand my intentions and misinterpret my actions.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am well aware of your intentions, Mr. Darcy, and I assure you that I do not misinterpret them.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, Elizabeth, that I find it quite distressing to be thus rejected by someone whom I had esteemed as a potential partner in life.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am not distressed by your rejection of me, Mr. Darcy, for I have never considered you a suitable partner in life. My feelings towards you have always been those of dislike and resentment, and I will not be swayed by empty words or grand gestures. I will not be trifled with.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must insist that you reconsider your refusal, Elizabeth. My esteem for you is genuine, and I am not one to be easily deterred by rebuff.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I must be clear, Mr. Darcy, that my refusal is not a matter of reconsideration, but of conviction. Your past behavior towards me and others has earned my distrust, and I will not be swayed by your words alone.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, Elizabeth, that I find your vehemence quite distressing, and I begin to wonder if your affections are not as indifferent as you claim. Your words, though sharp, reveal a depth of feeling that I had not previously suspected.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: In vain have I struggled. It will not do. My feelings will not be repressed. You must allow me to tell you how ardently I admire and love you.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: In such cases as this, it is, I believe, the established mode to express a sense of obligation for the sentiments avowed, however unequally they may be returned. It is natural that obligation should be felt, and if I could feel gratitude, I would now thank you. But I cannot--I have never desired your good opinion, and you have certainly bestowed it most unwillingly. I am sorry to have occasioned pain to anyone. It has been most unconsciously done, however, and I hope will be of short duration. The feelings which you tell me have long prevented the acknowledgment of your regard can have little difficulty in overcoming it after this explanation.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: And this is all the reply which I am to have the honour of expecting! I might, perhaps, wish to be informed why, with so little endeavour at civility, I am thus rejected. But it is of small importance.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I might as well inquire, why, with so evident a design of offending and insulting me, you chose to tell me that you liked me against your will, against your reason, and even against your character? Was not this some excuse for incivility, if I was uncivil? But I have other provocations. You know I have. Had not my own feelings decided against you, had they been indifferent, or had they even been favourable, do you think that any consideration would tempt me to accept the man who has been the means of ruining, perhaps for ever, the happiness of a most beloved sister?

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I have every reason in the world to think ill of you. No motive can excuse the unjust and ungenerous part you acted there. You dare not, you cannot deny that you have been the principal, if not the only means of dividing them from each other, of exposing one to the censure of the world for caprice and instability, the other to its derision for disappointed hopes, and involving them both in misery of the acutest kind.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Can you deny that you have done it?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: I have no wish of denying that I did everything in my power to separate my friend from your sister, or that I rejoice in my success. Towards him I have been kinder than towards myself.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: But it is not merely this affair, on which my dislike is founded. Long before it had taken place, my opinion of you was decided. Your character was unfolded in the recital which I received many months ago from Mr. Wickham. On this subject, what can you have to say? In what imaginary act of friendship can you here defend yourself? or under what misrepresentation can you here impose upon others?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: You take an eager interest in that gentleman’s concerns.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Who that knows what his misfortunes have been can help feeling an interest in him?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: yes, his misfortunes have been great indeed.
